prompt: A 4x3 grid of twelve separate small advertisement illustrations, each filling its cell edge to edge, in the style of 1960s Japanese Showa-era train poster art: flat silkscreen colours, limited palette, slight paper grain, bold simple shapes. Absolutely no text, no letters, no numbers, no logos anywhere. No borders, no gaps, no lines between cells. Row 1: (1) a sandy Baltic beach with striped umbrellas and a small green-and-cream train running on rails just under the sea toward a little island with pines; (2) a red cable-car cabin gliding on a wire over a seaside town of five-storey apartment blocks; (3) a glowing beige 1980s home computer and CRT monitor with a joystick on a desk, warm lamp; (4) a kiosk window with a bottle of lemonade and a vanilla ice cream cone on a waffle. Row 2: (5) a bakery basket with a round rye loaf and braided sweet buns; (6) polished honey-coloured Baltic amber pendants on dark velvet; (7) a murmuration of starlings forming a swirl over the sea at sunset; (8) a scientist in a white coat at a blackboard with a model atom and a telescope, retro science lecture. Row 3: (9) a tin of smoked sprats with golden fish fanned out, lemon and rye bread; (10) a wooden 1960s radio-gramophone set with a vinyl record; (11) fireworks over a calm sea at night with a pier; (12) a steaming public bathhouse with a painted Mount Fuji mural and wooden buckets.
